_comment: The PINNED operating point. Changing any value here changes the number, so a change must come with a re-run and a new committed result. run.py stamps the config it actually used into every result file, so a number can never be read without its operating point.

dataset.name: locomo10
dataset._redistribution: NOT redistributed here (LOCOMO is not ours to ship). Download locomo10.json, then either put it in benchmarks/locomo/data/ or point --data / $INSPEXIMUS_LOCOMO_PATH at it. When it is absent run.py SKIPS with a reason and exit code 3; it never scores on a substitute. A file whose sha256 differs from the pin is refused unless --allow-dataset-drift is passed, and the run is then stamped dataset_drift=true.

question_filter._categories_note: category 5 is LOCOMO's adversarial/unanswerable class and is excluded, exactly as in probes/retrieval_recall_locomo.py.

small._note: conversation 0 only. Retrieval recall runs on ALL of its answerable questions (LLM-free); end-to-end QA runs on the first qa_max_questions in dataset order. Sized to survive on a GPU shared with other processes.

medium._note: three conversations, 20 QA questions each (60 judged questions x 6 arms = 720 answer+judge pairs). The headline end-to-end number: wide enough that one flipped judgement is not 5 points, small enough to finish inside one quiesced-GPU window.

full._note: all 10 conversations, all 1536 answerable questions -- the exact denominator of the published retrieval pair. Use --retrieval-only: the end-to-end half at this size is ~18000 model calls and needs many hours of a quiesced GPU.

retrieval._reinforce_note: recall() defaults to reinforce=True, which mutates value/last_access and therefore makes recall ORDER-DEPENDENT. The published probe ran with that default. The harness PINS reinforce=false so a re-run is deterministic, and ALSO measures the reinforce=true arm so the published pair is compared like for like.

qa._judge_note: The judge is deliberately a different model family from the answerer (Meta vs Alibaba) so an answer is never graded by its own author. ONE judge grades every arm, so the arms are comparable even where the absolute number is judge-dependent. It must clear judge_calibration.py before any number is trusted.
qa._budget_note: Every retrieval-based arm gets the SAME 6000-char budget -- an unmatched budget is what flipped the ranking in benchmarks/memops (9x gap, accuracy 0.28 -> 0.59). fullcontext is the ceiling arm and is allowed the whole conversation by definition; its realised context size is recorded per item so the asymmetry is visible rather than assumed.
qa._workers_note: SAY THE PARALLELISM OUT LOUD. This was an inherited default of 4 living only in a .get() call, which is how a run silently goes 7x slower than the box can do. Measured serially 2026-08-24: qwen3.8:27b answers at 0.279 calls/s, so 18,432 calls is 18.4 h; at 4 workers 0.693 calls/s = 7.4 h. It is 4 and not higher because the two phases keep ONE 16.2 GB model resident on a 24 GB card -- the workers share that single resident model, and raising this does not load a second one, it only deepens the queue in front of the first.
qa._cap_note: A CAP IS A MODEL FILTER, and these were 80 and 8. Measured 2026-08-24 on one identical one-word question: qwen3.8:27b, gemma4:12b and ornith-1.5:9b all returned EMPTY with finish_reason=length at a 24-token cap and answered correctly at 500, needing 30, 80 and 37 completion tokens to emit the word 'Blue'. qwen2.5:7b needed 2 and was the only model the old caps admitted, which is why it kept winning our benchmarks. Every current model spends its first tokens on hidden reasoning, so a tight cap excludes the entire generation. Brevity is the PROMPT's job ('Answer in as few words as possible'); the cap exists only to stop a runaway. Raising it does not move a non-thinking model: qwen2.5:7b returns the same 2-token answer at 24 and at 500.

band._note: The three comparison arms under ONE judge. inspeximus must land STRICTLY between the naive-recency floor and the full-context ceiling. A band violation is reported, not tuned away: retrieval beating a stuffed context is a real result, and so is retrieval failing to beat last-k.

controls._note: Independent of the band: the checks that decide whether ANY number may be published. If a floor scores well or the ceiling scores badly, the harness is measuring something other than memory and run.py says BROKEN instead of printing a score.
controls._floor_shuffled_note: allowed a higher bound than floor_empty because a deranged context is still drawn from the SAME conversation and can contain the answer by luck; it is a conservative floor, not a loose one.

judge_gate._note: Same shape as benchmarks/memops/judge_calibration.py: three arms, >=90% each, or the run is void.

gpu._note: HARD pre-flight. The harness never kills anything -- a coordinator owns process lifecycle -- it refuses to start. --allow-shared-gpu overrides it and stamps gpu.contended=true on the result so a contended number can never be read as a quiesced one.
gpu._min_free_note: MEASURED, not rounded. The card is 24576 MiB and this is a workstation: the desktop compositor and browsers hold ~4.4 GB that no benchmark can reclaim, so with brain, dungeon and every foreign runner stopped the most that was ever observed free is 21034 MiB. The first version of this gate asked for 20480 free AFTER our own three models had loaded (~15.4 GB), which no state of this machine can satisfy -- a threshold that cannot be crossed is not a gate. 18000 is above what our own models need plus a real margin, and still refuses if another ~2.5 GB job appears. The check compares against effective_free = free + VRAM held by OUR OWN pinned models (read from Ollama's /api/ps), because otherwise a second run is refused for the memory the first run is legitimately holding.
gpu._runner_note: A runner launched from inside the Ollama installation is OURS -- on Windows llama-server.exe IS how Ollama runs a model, and a rule that simply forbade that name forbade our own inference backend and could never pass. A runner started from anywhere else is another job competing for the same card, and that is what this refuses on.
gpu._drift_note: The card is sampled at the START and the END of every run and the two are diffed. Sampling only at the start is how a run gets certified clean and then measured dirty: on 2026-08-02 a Windows scheduled task restarted two ~20 GB services mid-run, the pre-flight had already stamped contended=false, and the only symptom was per-call latency going from 2.6 s to 75 s before the inference server died. A VRAM drop larger than what our own models account for, by more than this many MiB, means something else took the card and the run spans two regimes.
gpu._cache_hit_note: A 0.0 s reply is a CACHE HIT, not a call. Replies faster than this are counted and reported, never averaged away.

tolerance._note: A re-run must land inside these bands or the committed result is stale / the run is contaminated. Set from MEASURED run-to-run spread, not guessed -- see README.md, 'Tolerance, and where it comes from'.

published_reference._what: The number this harness exists to make reproducible.
published_reference.cited_in: README.md 'And it doesn't cost you recall'; CHANGELOG.md 1.11.0 (0.783/0.648), flagged in 1.54.0 as 'reported, not independently reproducible from this repo'

_config_version_note: v2 (2026-08-24) raised answer_max_tokens 80 -> 512 and judge_max_tokens 8 -> 256 so a model that thinks before answering can be measured at all. Results produced under v1 used the old caps; for qwen2.5:7b and llama3.1:8b they are unaffected (neither reaches the old cap), but a v1 result is not comparable to a v2 result taken with any thinking model.
